title: Appraisal

title: Appraisal Dimension

title: Arc Sample

summary: The interpretive type of a character arc — a VALUE vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses). Coming-of-age, redemption, and fall are examples; the set is open.
title: Arc Type

summary: A written work published in a periodical, blog, or scholarly venue. A specialization of gmeow:Work.
title: Article

summary: An articulation or attack quality applied to a ToneEvent — staccato, legato, tenuto, accent, marcato, pizzicato, harmonic, etc. A value vocabulary of individuals; never subclassed (Principle 9).
title: Articulation Kind

summary: An observation that scores a target against a criterion (or whole rubric) — vantage = the judge, human or model: an LLM judge is just a vantage, and two models disagreeing are two coexisting cells with no winner (Principle 9). The judge model's identity and prompt digest travel as observation provenance. gmeow:assessm...
title: Assessment

summary: A financial asset — a stock, bond, cryptocurrency, real estate holding, commodity, or other instrument of value. The thing that is held, not the holding itself (which is a Holding relator).
title: Asset

summary: The kind of a financial asset — a VALUE, never an Asset subclass. Open vocabulary.
title: Asset Type

summary: A single ODRL constraint comparison: a gmeow:leftOperand (the dimension tested), a gmeow:constraintOperator (the comparison), and a gmeow:rightOperand (the value). E.g. leftOperand dateTime, operator lteq, rightOperand 2030-01-01 — 'valid until 2030'.
title: Atomic Constraint

summary: A non-inline body part presented as an attached file. An attachment may also be a gmeow:Document or gmeow:MediaObject (the two are not disjoint), and its text extraction or summary is a derived object linked by gmeow:wasDerivedFrom.
title: Attachment

summary: A reified assertion envelope that an attester vouches for a claim, artifact, identity binding, process, quality report, or ledger claim under a specific policy. Mediates between an attester, an attested subject, and optionally an attested claim or artifact. Distinct from Observation: an attestation is a vouching act,...
title: Attestation

summary: A concrete carrier of an attestation — in-toto JSON, SLSA provenance, W3C Verifiable Credential, DSSE envelope, C2PA manifest, EAT token, signed RDF graph, SCITT signed statement, nanopublication, signed git tag, release manifest, or signed blockchain payload. title: Attestation Artifact

summary: The policy or framework under which an attestation was issued — a value vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses). Open-ended; specific policies are minted as needed.
title: Attestation Policy

summary: The kind of attestation being made — a value vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses). title: Attestation Type

summary: The outcome of an email authentication check (RFC 8601 Authentication-Results) — a method (DKIM, SPF, DMARC, ARC), a verdict, and the verifying server.
title: Authentication Result

summary: A recorded author or committer string in a version-control commit — the raw git bytes (Name <email>). This is the immutable historical assertion, independent of the current canonical agent. Superseded identities are retained with gmeow:displayable false rather than deleted (Principle 10).
title: Author Identity

summary: The claimed authority grade of a norm within its issuing system — an ordered value vocabulary (absolute ≻ high ≻ medium ≻ conditional), the kernel GranularityLevel pattern. title: Availability

summary: The availability state of an agent over a time slot — a VALUE vocabulary aligned to iCalendar VFREEBUSY, never a subclass.
title: Availability Status

summary: A coordinate axis or dimension of a reference frame (e.g. X, Y, Z, latitude, longitude, elevation, time).

summary: A parent-child relationship by biological descent.

summary: A content-addressed blob of raw file content — the leaf of a Merkle source tree, independent of filename or path. Aligned to git blob objects and Software Heritage Content by reference. A Blob is the bytes only; the name is carried by the TreeEntry that points to it.

summary: A block of transactions on a distributed ledger or blockchain.

summary: An annotation that records a target resource for later retrieval, motivated by bookmarking. Typically has no body and no selector (the target entity itself is the bookmarked resource).

summary: A mutable pointer to a line of development in a repository — a named reference that advances as new commits are added. An InformationObject, not an Event or Entity.
title: Branch

summary: The kind of guard condition on a control-flow edge — a VALUE, never a subclass. Evaluated solver-side (Principle 12). The set is open; new condition kinds are fresh individuals.
title: Branch Condition Type

summary: A software build process that transforms source code into one or more distribution artifacts. title: Build Activity

summary: The build system or agent that performs a BuildActivity — e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Buildkite, or a local make invocation. A SoftwareAgent scoped to the build role.
title: Builder

title: Cadastral Reference

title: Cadastral Reference Type

summary: A CalDAV-style collection of scheduled events — an information object that aggregates calendar members and carries a default time zone. The container, not the contents.
title: Calendar

title: Calendar Method

summary: The rules mapping a time scale to human-readable dates. Co-equal: Gregorian is one peer among Julian, Hebrew, Islamic, Chinese, Persian, Ethiopian, Coptic, ISO week, and others (Principle 9).
title: Calendar System

summary: A measurement of the maximum number of entities a location can hold. The location is the observedFeature; the result is a ScalarQuantity. title: Capacity

summary: The medium of a physical carrier — a VALUE vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses). Print, e-ink file, optical disc, and server object are examples; the set is open.
title: Carrier Medium

summary: A point on the celestial sphere expressed as right ascension, declination, and an optional epoch — frame-relative per Principle 11. The reference frame (ICRS, FK5, Galactic, etc.) is declared via gmeow:coordinateFrame.

summary: An astronomical location — a position on the celestial sphere, a solar-system body, a spacecraft, or a deep-sky object. title: Celestial Location

summary: The origin of a celestial coordinate system (topocentric, geocentric, barycentric, heliocentric, etc.). A value vocabulary aligned to IVOA refposition.

summary: A reified attestation that a cryptographic key belongs to a given identity, made by a certifying agent (a PGP key-signature / Web-of-Trust certification). Its validity window is carried with gmeow:validFrom/validUntil; revocation sets validUntil.

summary: A first-class interpretive/structural information object describing a character's trajectory through a narrative — a standpoint-scoped analysis, never canonical truth. summary: A contiguous segment of a source information object, produced by a chunking step for retrieval — the unit a retrieval returns, a model reads, and an evidence span pins into. summary: The veridicality status of a claim — whether it is untrue, licensed-false (fiction, satire, sarcasm), or true. summary: The event of reviewing code changes for quality, correctness, and policy compliance — an event (not an Activity, because reviewing is observation-like) with a reviewer, a merge request or commit under review, and an outcome. summary: The capability class of a transform codec — encode, compress, or encrypt (spec §8). Determines the degradation path when the capability is missing: unknown-codec or missing-key opacity.

summary: An aggregation of resources. A specialization of gmeow:Work.
title: Collection

summary: A version-control commit — a content-addressed provenance event that records a change to a repository's history. summary: A graph-clustering community (Leiden or similar) over extracted-entity descriptions, at a level (gmeow:communityLevel) of the cluster hierarchy. The clustering run is provenance via the EXISTING gmeow:wasGeneratedBy.
title: Community

summary: A pre-generated summary of a community — GraphRAG's global-question substrate, gmeow:wasDerivedFrom the community's members and chunks and gmeow:wasGeneratedBy its generating invocation (EXISTING provenance), hence revisable rather than a black box.
title: Community Summary

summary: An observation that an event complied with or violated a norm — vantage = the assessor. The reified form of gmeow:violates / gmeow:complies, for when who-judged, on-what-evidence, and how-confidently must be first-class. title: Condition

summary: An observation that a condition held, did not hold, or could not be determined at some moment — vantage = the evaluator (an agent, a solver run, a model). title: Condition Evaluation

summary: A machine formalization of a condition in a named expression language. Attaching one to a Condition (gmeow:formalizedAs) is a claim that the expression captures...
title: Condition Expression

summary: A composite condition — all-of, any-of, or none-of its members (arbitrary and/or/not trees by nesting groups). Requires an operator and at least two members (SHACL). A group is itself a Condition: it carries its own prose summary and can be evaluated, formalized, and reused like any other.
title: Condition Group

summary: A named binding that instantiates a condition template — 'threshold = 0.8', 'jurisdiction = Canada'. Lets one Condition serve many norms with different bindings.
title: Condition Parameter

summary: A policy conflict-resolution strategy — the ODRL conflict values perm / prohibit / invalid.
title: Conflict Strategy

summary: A reified traversable link between two entities, able to bear its own period, cost, weight, bandwidth, confidence, and standpoint. The flat shortcut is gmeow:connectsTo; promote to Connection when metadata matters.
title: Connection

summary: The abstract base of a condition on a rights rule (odrl:Constraint) — specialised by gmeow:AtomicConstraint (a leftOperand / operator / rightOperand comparison, e.g. dateTime ≤ 2030, spatial = EU, count ≤ 5) and gmeow:LogicalConstraint (a boolean combination of constraints). A licence's temporal bound is an AtomicCons...
title: Constraint

summary: The boolean operator of a logical constraint — odrl:and / odrl:or / odrl:xone (exactly one) / odrl:andSequence (ordered conjunction).
title: Constraint Logic

summary: The comparison operator of an atomic constraint — the ODRL operator vocabulary (eq, neq, lt, lteq, gt, gteq, isPartOf, isA, isAnyOf, …).
title: Constraint Operator

summary: A means of reaching an agent: an email address, telephone number, or postal address.
title: Contact Point

summary: The usage role of a contact point — a VALUE vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses). Personal, work, personal-domain, support, billing, and emergency are examples; the set is open. Projects to schema:contactType and the vCard TYPE parameter.
title: Contact Point Type

summary: The reified, time-scoped fact that a place was contained in a larger place over an interval — for boundary changes, re-organisations, and disputed parallel parents. Reifies containedInPlace over time; the plain transitive property remains the flat shortcut.
title: Containment Tenure

summary: The presentation disposition of a body part — inline (displayed as part of the message body) or attachment (presented as a separate file). An open value vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses).
title: Content Disposition

summary: Records that two agents have worked together; symmetric. The period is carried with gmeow:validFrom/validUntil on the statement, or reified as a gmeow:ProfessionalRelationship.

summary: The entity in which this hazard inheres. Functional and mandatory (SHACL): a disposition has exactly one bearer (gUFO inherence, asserted with GMEOW's own property — Principle 5). The same danger borne by two systems is two hazards.

summary: The hazard's graded severity, when graded standalone (a hazard feeding a cascade usually inherits attention from the cascade's grade). NOT functional (PR #385 review — evaluative, source-variable; the hasAuthorityLevel convention); optional, at most one per base graph (SHACL).
title: hazard severity

summary: The field name of a message header.
title: header name

summary: The field value of a message header.
title: header value

summary: The compass direction an entity is facing, typically clockwise from north, in degrees.
title: heading

summary: The standpoint claim that the deceiver actually holds to be true — the private belief or position that contrasts with the projected standpoint in a deception event. Non-functional: a complex deception may involve multiple held standpoints.
title: held standpoint

summary: The agent that holds the asset. Functional: a holding is held by exactly one agent.
title: holding agent

summary: The financial asset that is held. Functional: a holding is of exactly one asset.
title: holding asset

summary: The cost basis of the holding — the original monetary amount paid to acquire the asset. Functional: a holding has one canonical cost basis (disputed values are standpoint-indexed claims).

summary: The time interval over which the holding is valid. Optional: omit for point-in-time holdings.
title: holding period

summary: The quantity of the asset held, as an xsd:decimal. Functional: a holding has exactly one quantity at a given point in time (competing standpoint-indexed quantities coexist as separate statements).
title: holding quantity

summary: Relates an agent to an online account it holds.
title: holds account

summary: Relates an agent to a credential it holds. Non-functional — an agent may hold many credentials, and a single credential may be held by many agents (shared license, group certification).

summary: An honorific/title of address for a person (a gmeow:Honorific value). Non-functional and contextual. A form of ADDRESS, sex/gender-independent — MUST NOT be inferred from gender identity/expression, sex-assigned-at-birth or orientation.

summary: The domain/class of an honorific (academic, clerical, noble, military, judicial, social).

summary: Whether an honorific is rendered before (prefix) or after (suffix) the name.
title: honorific position

summary: The position of a hop within the message path (1 = closest to the origin).

summary: The forge or hosting platform where a repository is hosted. Non-functional: a repository may be mirrored on multiple platforms.
title: hosted at

summary: Term-level advisory metadata carrying a short modeling recipe for the HOW facet: the companion properties, relators, statement metadata, or projection checks that normally travel with the annotated term. Documentation-only; it does not change OWL entailments.
title: how to use

summary: A formal identifier of a creative work, such as a DOI or patent number.

summary: The scheme of an identifier — e.g. 'lei', 'ror', 'naics', 'isicV4', 'companyRegistration', 'wikidata'. Declared on the Identifier node, not the Organization, to avoid cross-product pairing bugs when multiple identifiers coexist.

summary: The authority URL that resolves an identifier record — e.g. the geni profile page, the ORCID record URL, the ROR landing page. The resolvable counterpart of the scheme-local gmeow:identifierValue; projects to schema:PropertyValue/url. Range is intentionally open (an IRI).

summary: The literal value of an identifier — e.g. '529900T8BM49AURSDO55' or '541511'.

summary: The raw Importance header value of an email message (high, normal, or low). Stored as the canonical header literal; the vocabulary is small but client-extensible.

summary: The reference assembly (e.g. GRCh38) in which these sequence coordinates are expressed. Functional: a coordinate tuple is expressed in exactly one assembly; coordinates in another assembly are a different SequenceCoordinates instance (Principle 11).

summary: The approximate-nearest-neighbour structure this index uses (open vocabulary).

summary: The build parameters (efConstruction, nlist, M, ...) recorded verbatim as a JSON object string — reproducibility provenance; their semantics stay in the solver layer (P12).

summary: Relates an organization to an industry-classification identifier — a NAICS, ISIC, or schema.org industry code. The scheme is declared via gmeow:identifierScheme on the Identifier node. Non-functional: multiple classifications may coexist.

summary: When an import activity recorded its claims into the system — the transaction time. Distinct from gmeow:assertedAt (observation) and gmeow:validFrom/validUntil (validity).

summary: The priority of a research inquiry, on a 1–10 scale. Applies to Procedures of type researchPlan.

summary: The status of a research inquiry, drawn from the gmeow:ExecutionStatus value vocabulary. Applies to Procedures of type researchPlan. Non-functional: competing assessments coexist.

summary: The thematic area or topic of a research inquiry. Applies to Procedures of type researchPlan. Open vocabulary — any literal is valid.

summary: The physical object that bears an inscription. Functional: an inscription is borne by exactly one carrier (if a copy exists on another carrier, it is a distinct Inscription instance).

summary: The agent in whom a desire or intention inheres. Functional: an intrinsic mode has exactly one bearer (gUFO inherence, asserted with GMEOW's own property by Principle 5 — gufo:inheresIn is the alignment target, not the asserted axiom). Two agents wanting the same goal are two modes sharing one gmeow:intentionGoal.

summary: The goal at which a desire, intention, or commitment aims — its propositional content. Functional: one mode, one goal; an agent pursuing five goals bears five modes. Sharing is at the Goal: two agents committed to the same outcome hold distinct modes aiming at one Goal individual.

summary: The interpolation mode between control points (linearCents, exponential, stochasticByReference).

summary: An optional free-text note recording an intersex variation, for inclusivity where gmeow:sexAssignedAtBirth gmeow:saabIntersex is insufficient. Deliberately a plain note, NOT a clinical DSD taxonomy and NOT a value vocabulary — GMEOW does not model medical sex characteristics in depth.

summary: Allen AFTER: this interval begins strictly after the related interval ends. Transitive inverse of gmeow:intervalBefore. (= time:intervalAfter)

summary: Allen DURING: this interval's extent falls strictly within the related interval's extent. Transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalContains. (= time:intervalDuring)

summary: Allen FINISHED-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalFinishes. (= time:intervalFinishedBy)

summary: Allen MEETS: this interval ends exactly when the related interval begins. NOT transitive. Inverse of gmeow:intervalMetBy. (= time:intervalMeets)

summary: Allen MET-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalMeets. (= time:intervalMetBy)

summary: Allen OVERLAPPED-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalOverlaps. (= time:intervalOverlappedBy)

summary: Allen STARTED-BY: inverse of gmeow:intervalStarts. (= time:intervalStartedBy)

summary: The trust-signature amount/weight the trustor assigns to the trustee as an introducer.

summary: The total monetary amount requested by the invoice, expressed as a MonetaryAmount. Functional: an invoice has one canonical total amount.

summary: The status of an invoice, drawn from the open InvoiceStatus value vocabulary. Non-functional: an invoice may progress through several statuses over time.

summary: Whether the licence is approved by the Open Source Initiative (spdx:isOsiApproved).

summary: Whether the asset is accessible without payment (schema:isAccessibleForFree).

summary: The instant an attestation was issued. Functional: the issue time is constitutive of the attestation's identity.

summary: The item an offering provides — a gmeow:ServiceOffering, a product, or any entity. Projects to schema:itemOffered.

summary: The postings that compose a journal entry. Non-functional: a journal entry has at least two postings (SHACL-enforced).

summary: The key's algorithm (e.g. rsa, ed25519, secp256k1). Not functional (source-variable).

summary: A short identifier for a key (e.g. a PGP long key id). Not functional (source-variable).

summary: The public key material itself (armored or hex form). Not functional (encodings vary by source).
title: key material

summary: The scheme/format of a cryptographic key (one of the gmeow:KeyScheme individuals). Functional: a key has exactly one scheme — a key of a different scheme is a different key.

summary: Relates an agent to a language it knows. Non-functional. The leveled, per-skill detail is carried by the reified gmeow:LanguageProficiency.

summary: The sensory/transmission modality/modalities of a language (gmeow:LanguageModality individuals). Non-functional — many languages are multimodal (spoken and written).

summary: The origin kind(s) of a language (gmeow:LanguageOrigin individuals). Non-functional — a contact language may be both creole and mixed.

summary: The dimension an atomic constraint tests — one of the gmeow:LeftOperand values (odrl:leftOperand). Functional.

summary: Relates an organization to a legal identifier — a LEI, ROR ID, company-registration number, or other scheme-specific code. The scheme is declared via gmeow:identifierScheme on the Identifier node. Non-functional: an organization may have several legal identifiers.

summary: The scale a proficiency-level individual belongs to (e.g. cefrB2 levelScale scaleCEFR). Functional.
